reference.source: Volpe's Neurology of the Newborn / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A posterior fossa malformation defined by hypoplasia or agenesis of the cerebellar vermis, cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle communicating with the cyst, and an enlarged posterior fossa with upward displacement of the tentorium and torcula
Hydrocephalus is common but often develops after the neonatal period rather than at birth
It should be distinguished from milder posterior fossa variants such as an isolated mega cisterna magna or a Blake pouch cyst, which have a different prognosis
It may be isolated or associated with other central nervous system anomalies such as agenesis of the corpus callosum, and with chromosomal and single-gene syndromes
Presentation ranges from an incidental finding to macrocephaly, developmental delay, hypotonia, ataxia, and signs of raised intracranial pressure
Neurodevelopmental outcome depends strongly on the presence of associated brain malformations and any underlying genetic syndrome rather than the posterior fossa cyst alone
Diagnosis is by prenatal ultrasound and foetal or postnatal MRI, with genetic evaluation when other anomalies coexist
reference.pathophysiology: Dandy-Walker malformation arises from abnormal development of the cerebellar vermis and the roof of the fourth ventricle in early gestation. Failure of normal vermian formation and of the developing fourth ventricular roof leads to cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle that balloons into an enlarged posterior fossa, elevating the tentorium and torcula. Disturbed cerebrospinal fluid dynamics predispose to hydrocephalus. The malformation may occur in isolation or as part of chromosomal, single-gene, or teratogenic disorders, and coexisting supratentorial anomalies largely determine the neurological outcome.
additionalDifferentials: Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia of other cause including Joubert syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to characterise the vermis, fourth ventricle, and posterior fossa and to distinguish it from milder variants
Prenatal ultrasound and foetal MRI when suspected antenatally
Chromosomal microarray and, where indicated, exome sequencing
Evaluation for associated supratentorial and systemic anomalies
Serial head circumference measurement and imaging to monitor for hydrocephalus
Developmental assessment and neurosurgical review if hydrocephalus develops
redFlags: Progressive hydrocephalus with raised intracranial pressure requiring neurosurgical intervention
Rapidly increasing head circumference in an infant
Apnoea or brainstem signs from posterior fossa mass effect
Multiple associated anomalies suggesting a serious underlying syndrome
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies widely. Isolated Dandy-Walker malformation with a normally formed vermis apart from the cyst can have a favourable neurodevelopmental outcome, whereas cases with vermian agenesis, associated brain malformations, or a genetic syndrome often have significant developmental disability.
pitfalls: Overdiagnosing Dandy-Walker malformation when the finding is actually a benign mega cisterna magna or Blake pouch cyst
Giving a uniformly poor prognosis without assessing for associated anomalies and genetic cause
Assuming hydrocephalus is always present at birth and not monitoring for its later development
Neglecting a full genetic and structural evaluation in apparently isolated cases
management: Treat hydrocephalus neurosurgically when it develops, typically with cerebrospinal fluid shunting (ventriculoperitoneal shunt) or endoscopic third ventriculostomy, sometimes with cyst fenestration
Monitor with serial head circumference measurement and neuroimaging for the development of hydrocephalus and raised intracranial pressure
Provide developmental support and early intervention with physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech therapy for delay, hypotonia and ataxia
Treat associated seizures with antiepileptic drugs where epilepsy occurs
Investigate for associated brain malformations and genetic syndromes with chromosomal microarray and, where indicated, exome sequencing, as these largely determine outcome
Offer genetic counselling and, where a syndrome or teratogenic cause is identified, family and reproductive counselling
Coordinate multidisciplinary follow-up with neurology, neurosurgery and developmental services
